## Triage: first grade, `priority:p2` · `domain:services` · `area:workflow` · `pm:queue` (`finding` removed). Direction: `get_record` asks the engine for `id` itself

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-08T20:07Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `packages/services/service-automation` (`builtin/crud-nodes.ts`, `get_record`'s `findOne` branch) ⇒ `domain:services`. Rationale: `packages/services/*` belongs to that lane.

- **Why p2:** a declared node output reads `undefined` with no error, so a downstream node acts on nothing.
  - On `main`, it reaches the SQL driver family whenever the author narrows `fields` without `id`.
  - PR #22337 widens that to every driver.
  - It is read from source only, so measure first, as the card says.
- **Direction:** the card's own. `get_record` includes `id` in the projection it hands the engine. Record in the PR whether `record` then carries `id` when the author did not name it.
- **Pins:** on a SQL driver, with `fields` that omit `id`, `output.id` is the row's id.
  - Control: with no `fields`, the output is unchanged.
  - ⛔ No change to PR #22337's engine-level trimming.
- **Not blocked:** the defect is on `main` today, independent of PR #22337. If both change the same test fixture, rebase on whichever lands first.

**Executes triage's direction** (`6068120223`): `get_record` includes `id` in the projection it hands the engine, so `output.id` no longer depends on the author's `fields`. Measure first; the card is read from source.

File surface at `origin/main` `35afb158`:
- **`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts`:** `get_record`'s `findOne` branch, the projection it hands `serveFamilyRead` and the engine.
- **Tests and changeset:** tests in `service-automation` and one `@objectstack/service-automation` `patch` changeset.
  - The pin: on a SQL driver, with `fields` that omit `id`, `output.id` is the row's id.
  - Control: with no `fields`, the output is unchanged.
  - Whether `record` then carries `id` when the author did not name it is recorded in the PR.

Exclusions:
- ⛔ No change to PR #22337's engine-level trimming (`objectql`, `domain:engine`).
- ⛔ No `packages/spec`.
- ⛔ The `find` branch (`limit > 1`) is unchanged: it declares no top-level `id`.

Stop on breach; explain in the report.
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (`dispatch-gates --tier`: no path-derived mandate; default tier)
Clause-②: no
- A declared node output (`get_record`'s `id`) is honoured: no accept set or public signature moves.
Responsibility: `this repository's own code: get_record hands the author's fields to the engine unchanged and reads output.id from the result, so a projection without id answers undefined | none: no layer adds id to a narrowed projection on the SQL drivers | flow authors who narrow get_record's fields and reference the node's id downstream`
Thread-read: 6068120223
Serial constraints cleared:
- No open PR touches `crud-nodes.ts`. PR #22337 (`domain:engine`) adds `builtin/get-record-formula-projection.integration.test.ts` (declared on #6021, `6066696545`); if both change one fixture, the later rebases on the earlier.

## Seat ACCEPT: PR #22355 at `f68b7d55c5` · seat `domain:services#1` (#6021) · `session_01WkL6Eijt432S1Y7ekb6ovQ` · 2026-10-08T21:43Z

Checked against GitHub and the branch, not the report's prose (`os-dev-report` `6069595763`).

- **Form:**
  - The PR is a draft. Its first line is `Fixes #22344`, with a line-start `Clause-②: no`. The PR assignee is `os-bill`.
  - Five files, +243/−5. `check-governed-merges --pr 22355`: NOT governed. It merges clean with `main`.
- **H1 reproduced on `main`, so the card stands as graded.** Through the real `ObjectQL` and the `get_record` executor, `fields: ['title']` answered `output.id` `undefined` on `driver-sql`, with the record carrying `title` only. `driver-memory` answered the id. A flow `get_record → update_record` filtering on `{read.id}` was refused for a condition that resolved to nothing.
- **The fix, read by the seat:**
  - `projectionNamingId(fields)` appends `id` to a non-empty projection that does not name it. It is applied at the `findOne` call site only, before `serveFamilyRead`, so the stored-metadata family door sees it as the node's own projection.
  - An absent or empty `fields` is still a whole-row read. A projection that already names `id` is handed over as written. The `find` branch (`limit > 1`) is untouched.
  - No `objectql` change: PR #22337's engine-level trimming is as it landed.
- **H2:** placing it inside the projection callback measured identical (23 of 23 on the ordinary and family paths). The shipped placement is the one that keeps the family door's view whole.
- **H3, accepted:** `record` carries the `id` the engine returned, so `{var.id}` through `outputVariable` agrees with `{read.id}`. Stripping it would be a second projection layer and would leave the same defect on the variable spelling.
- **Evidence:**
  - The new pin file was 2 red on `main`; it is 7 of 7 green with the fix.
  - The three `get_record` suites pass 23 of 23. `service-automation` passes 178 files and 2177 tests.
  - Ablations: reverting the fix turns 7 red; dropping the `includes('id')` guard hands the engine `['id','title','id']`; dropping the empty-list guard hands it `['id']`; making an absent `fields` name `id` turns 6 red. Each restore is proven. One no-op mutation was caught by `ablation-replace` and re-anchored.
  - Gates: 64 of 64 derived, with `--ran` a derived zero.
- **Deviations, accepted:**
  - `origin/main` was merged in, not rebased, after PR #22337 landed mid-run. Its new `get-record-formula-projection` test pinned the one-row column set exactly. Its one-row cases now expect `id`; its list cases and its engine trimming are unchanged. The file is in this lane's package, so no cross-lane declaration is owed. The `domain:engine` seat is told here, through this record on the card it noted.
  - The stored-metadata family suite's one-row body case now expects `id` beside the named columns; `type` is still dropped.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`:** two, noted and not filed:
  - `GetRecordConfigSchema.fields` in `packages/spec` reads "only these fields are read (default: all)", and the one-row branch now also reads `id`. That is wording, with no wrong runtime answer; a `domain:spec` pass on the node descriptors can carry it.
  - `driver-mongodb` was not measured. It is not a `service-automation` test dependency, and the fix is driver-independent.
- **Landing to-do:**
  - Every check on `f68b7d55c5` must be green or an expected skip.
  - Then ready and auto-merge through the relay, the merge-queue check, and the close-out.

**Landed** · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `session_01WkL6Eijt432S1Y7ekb6ovQ` · 2026-10-08T22:48Z.

PR #22355 merged through the merge queue as `43fc5005`. On `origin/main`, `@objectstack/service-automation` (`patch`):
- A `get_record` node's single-row branch names `id` in the projection it hands the engine, so `output.id` (and `{<node>.id}` downstream) is the row's id whatever `fields` names, on every driver.
- The served `record` carries that `id` beside the named columns, so the `outputVariable` spelling agrees.
- No `fields`, or an empty list, is still a whole-row read; a projection that names `id` is handed over as written; the multi-row branch is unchanged.

The PR's `Fixes` line closed the card `completed`. This note also removes `pm:dispatched` and the assignee.
- `GetRecordConfigSchema.fields`' description in `packages/spec` ("only these fields are read") does not mention `id`. That is wording only, left for a `domain:spec` pass on the node descriptors.
